reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Epithelioid macrophages with lymphocyte rim define a granuloma
Caseation strongly suggests tuberculosis but fungal infection can mimic it
Langhans giant cells arrange nuclei peripherally like a horseshoe
Granulation tissue is repair tissue, not a granuloma
reference.pathophysiology: Persistent stimuli recruit monocytes that become activated macrophages. T helper 1 cytokines, especially interferon gamma, organise macrophages into granulomas. Tumour necrosis factor maintains granuloma structure, which is why blocking it can reactivate latent tuberculosis.
additionalDifferentials: Foreign body reaction versus infective granuloma
additionalInvestigations: Ziehl Neelsen stain and mycobacterial culture or molecular testing
Fungal stains such as Gomori methenamine silver
Serum angiotensin converting enzyme as supportive, not diagnostic, evidence
